Loan loss reserves cannot exceed the loans they are held against
The allowance for loan and lease losses is a contra-asset and cannot be negative
Loans are a component of assets and cannot exceed the total
Total assets cannot be negative
A capital ratio cannot be negative

A tier 1 ratio above 1000pct is legitimate but rare -- a small bank holding almost only zero-risk-weight assets. NOT an error: the regulator's own reported ratio exceeds 1 for every one of these banks. See docs/QUALITY.md
Total capital includes tier 1 so its ratio cannot be smaller
Common equity tier 1 is a component of tier 1 capital
Risk-weighted assets far above total assets suggests a units or era-stitch error
Category charge-offs cannot exceed total charge-offs
Category recoveries cannot exceed total recoveries

Deposits exceed total assets only at an insolvent bank (negative equity). Before 1.3 it was written as dep_tot_dom <= assets and failed on 1,066 bank-quarters in every build, every one at a bank with negative equity: the 1986-91 savings-and-loan and real-estate losses, the 2009-11 financial crisis, and 2022-25 unrealized securities losses. The check was wrong, not the data. It now uses consolidated deposits.

The reported leverage ratio (after the automatic x100 / 1/100 unit correction) is within a factor of 30 of tier 1 capital over assets. A failure is a residual filer error the correction could not resolve -- for example tier 1 capital filed as zero next to a normal ratio.
The reported tier 1 ratio (after unit correction) is within a factor of 30 of tier1_capital / rwa.
The reported total capital ratio (after unit correction) is within a factor of 30 of total_capital / rwa.
The reported CET1 ratio (after unit correction) is within a factor of 30 of cet1 / rwa.
The reported tier 1 ratio is within 10% of tier1_capital / rwa. Both come from the same schedule, so a failure is a filing inconsistency worth a look (99.9% agree within 1%).
The reported CET1 ratio is within 10% of cet1 / rwa.
Tier 1 capital filed as exactly zero next to a positive leverage ratio: one of the two is a filing error (seen on the FR Y-9C).
Deposits are a component of total liabilities.

Loans gross of unearned income at or above loans net of it -- i.e. unearned income non-negative. NOT an invariant: a negative unearned-income line is filed by 0-0.04% of banks through 2022 and 0.6% by 2026 (net deferred loan costs), with differences of a few thousand dollars. Reported for information; see docs/QUALITY.md on checks that turn out to be wrong.
